items.name: Residual
items.when: Data minus fit, one entry per point. A fit is scored by $\|r\|^2$; the best fit makes it smallest.

items.name: Normal equations
items.when: To find the best fit. There is exactly one best line when $A^\mathsf{T}A$ is invertible.

items.name: Perpendicular check
items.when: To check a fit: dot $r$ with each column of $A$. At the best fit every one comes to 0.

items.name: Entries of AᵀA
items.when: To build $A^\mathsf{T}A$. It equals its own transpose, and its top-left entry is the number of points.

items.name: Entries of Aᵀb
items.when: To build the right-hand side. Add the products one at a time; addition slips are easy here.

items.name: A line of best fits
items.when: In the course's example (column 2 is $2 \times$ column 1) the normal equations say this twice. Every point on it is a best fit, all with $\|r\|^2 = 14$.

items.name: Null space
items.when: The directions $A$ can't see. Adding one to a best fit changes nothing $A$ can see.

items.name: Smallest best fit
items.when: Every best fit is $p + t\,d$ with $Ad = 0$. If $p \perp d$, the smallest one is at $t = 0$.

items.name: Singular values
items.when: The $\lambda_i$ are the eigenvalues of $A^\mathsf{T}A$, largest first. Its unit eigenvectors are the right singular vectors $v_i$.

items.name: Left singular vector
items.when: Where $A$ sends $v_1$, scaled to unit length: $A v_1 = \sigma_1 u_1$.

items.name: Pseudo-inverse from the SVD
items.when: To undo $A$ where it stretches, and send the direction it can't see to zero.

items.name: The 1/σ rule
items.formula: In $\Sigma^+$, each non-zero $\sigma$ becomes $1/\sigma$ and each zero stays $0$.
items.when: A zero singular value goes to zero, not to infinity.

items.name: The smallest best fit from A⁺
items.formula: $A^+ b$ is the smallest best fit. At rank 1: $A^+ b = \frac{1}{\sigma_1}(u_1 \cdot b)\,v_1$.
items.when: It has no part along a direction with $\sigma = 0$, and that is what makes it the smallest.

items.name: The easy half
items.when: $A_k$ is the SVD cut to $k$ terms. It reaches this error.

items.name: The hard half
items.formula: $\|A - B\|_2 \ge \sigma_{k+1}$ for every $B$ of rank at most $k$
items.when: So no matrix of rank at most $k$ does better than $A_k$ in the 2-norm.

items.name: The witness behind it
items.when: $w$ is a unit vector in both $N(B)$ and span$(v_1, \ldots, v_{k+1})$. Their dimensions add to $n + 1 > n$, so one exists.
